solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be assured of success in bespoke tailoring?

definitions.text: Be assured of success in bespoke tailoring?

parts.words: Be assured of success in bespoke tailoring?
parts.note: the idiom for being certain to succeed also literally describes ordering a suit to be cut to measure

explanation.surface: A tailor reflects that made-to-measure work is a guaranteed winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bespoke tailoring means having clothes made for you, which is exactly what the idiom says when read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to be sure of success, here reread literally as getting a garment produced to order.

clue.text: Work in garden keeps male in

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the gardening word contains the male letter

parts.note: to hoe is to work the soil in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener's labour keeps a man indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word: 'at home' means in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at one's house rather than out, as when someone is said to be in.

clue.text: With some courage turned round pointed item piercing barrel

indicators.note: piercing means going through, so the reversed item sits inside the barrel

parts.note: a vat is a large barrel or tub

indicators.note: turned round reverses the pointed item

parts.note: a nail is a pointed metal item

explanation.surface: Someone bravely drives a spike into a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and showing courage, so describing someone with a measure of pluck.

clue.text: Line taken from where SF is set, often offering a different view

indicators.note: the line letter is removed from the location phrase

parts.note: science fiction is often set on alien planets, in other worlds

explanation.surface: A sci-fi line lifted from an alien setting offers a fresh perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a restatement, putting something another way or from a fresh angle.

clue.text: I believe spirits may pen writing

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the spirits hold the writing word

parts.note: meths is methylated spirits
ink is the fluid used for writing

explanation.surface: A believer in ghosts thinks they may write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meths' is British for methylated spirits; 'pen' looks like writing but means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic expression meaning it seems to me, so a way of saying one believes.

clue.text: Activity in restaurant requiring much effort? Artist's failed to appear

indicators.note: the artist letters are absent from the effort word

parts.note: draining means exhausting, demanding much effort
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A tiring restaurant evening where the painter never showed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a meal is what customers do in a restaurant.

clue.text: Avoid taking stuff from bakery back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the bakery word from right to left

parts.note: small bread rolls or cakes sold by a baker are buns

explanation.surface: A dieter resolves to keep away from the baker's wares.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold-shoulder or pointedly ignore someone is to avoid them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Nasty moment, turning up amidst clamour

indicators.note: amidst puts the reversed moment inside the clamour

parts.note: clamour is loud noise

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reverses the moment word

explanation.surface: An unpleasant moment arrives in the middle of an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive or disgusting, especially in smell, so a synonym of nasty.

clue.text: Prow of boat in inlet — easy target for one with charge

indicators.note: in places the front letter within the inlet

parts.note: a bay is a coastal inlet

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so its first letter

parts.note: a sitter is an easy shot or target

explanation.surface: A boat moored in a bay makes a sitting duck for an attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks military but means a child in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking after children while parents are out has them as their charge.

clue.text: Unhappy being 'Prisoner X', taking refuge in whisky

indicators.note: the prisoner and the number hide inside the whisky word, as a fugitive shelters within

parts.note: malt is a kind of whisky
a con is a convict, a prisoner
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: An anonymous inmate drowns their sorrows in Scotch.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes someone discontented and dissatisfied, a synonym of unhappy.

clue.text: Meek individual with change of character becomes such a nuisance

indicators.note: one character, the letter A, is swapped for another, I

parts.note: a lamb is proverbially meek and gentle

explanation.surface: A mild person who changes personality turns into a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'limb' (short for 'limb of Satan') is an old-fashioned word for a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a naughty troublesome child, someone who is a pest.

clue.text: Mix of laconic and stoic, shattering received opinion

indicators.note: a mix of the two words blends their letters together

explanation.surface: A terse, impassive character upsets conventional thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Attacking cherished beliefs or established ideas, literally image-breaking.

clue.text: Disagreement about bunking off punishment

indicators.note: bunking off means skipping school, so the about letter goes missing

parts.note: a clash is a disagreement or conflict
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A row over truancy ends in a caning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunking off' is British slang for playing truant.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke of the whip given as a penalty, so a form of corporal punishment.

clue.text: Bar rings us, calling in copper without arousing suspicion

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a bar

indicators.note: calling in means visiting, so the copper drops in between the two rings

parts.note: two rings look like two letter Os
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A pub phones us after a policeman pops in, seemingly harmlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmless and inoffensive, so something that would not raise any alarm or concern.

clue.text: Gamble money earned from cleaning chimneys?

definitions.meaning: a lottery where entrants' stakes are pooled and paid out to the winners
read as a ..., the income of a chimney sweep

explanation.surface: A wager on what a chimney sweep might earn.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting pool with prizes drawn by lot, a kind of gamble; split it reads as the sweep's takings.

clue.text: Do this — and risk a wet splashing?

definitions.text: Do this — and risk a wet splashing?

indicators.note: splashing about stirs up the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: An invitation to a watersport that warns you may get drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashing' rearranges RISK A WET, and the whole clue also describes the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Being towed on skis behind a boat is an activity where getting soaked is a real prospect.

clue.text: Invade? Best to save force till later

indicators.note: the force letter is held back until a later position in the word

parts.note: finest means best
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: Advice to an army to keep its strength in reserve before an invasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till later' moves the F of FINEST further along.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a place in large numbers, as pests do, is a form of invading it.

clue.text: Celebrity upset about fire in the sky

indicators.note: the reversed celebrity goes around the fire word
in a down clue upset turns the celebrity word upside down, reversing it

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity
a pyre is a pile of wood set on fire

explanation.surface: A star is distraught over a blaze overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means heavenly or celestial, of the highest heaven, hence in the sky.

clue.text: College having change of heart after the writer rejected commission

indicators.note: after says the college word comes behind the rejected writer
rejected means thrown back, so the writer word is read in reverse

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, me

indicators.note: the central letters of the college word are rearranged, its heart altered

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of college

explanation.surface: A college reconsiders and turns down an author's commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer' is the setter speaking of themselves; 'College' is the old British polytechnic, whose heart letters swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: To commission someone is to engage or hire them for a job, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Harbour venue home to a particular person making discoveries

indicators.note: home to means housing, so the pier holds the particular word

parts.note: a pier is a structure in a harbour, often a seaside entertainment venue
one means a particular, as in 'one day'

explanation.surface: A seaside pier hosts a noted explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: An explorer or innovator who is first into new territory or ideas.

clue.text: Friendly enquiry doubting presence of wifi?

definitions.meaning: split as a question asking whether one is connected by a wire rather than wirelessly

explanation.surface: A cordial question from someone unsure whether wireless internet is available.
explanation.definitionFit: Means good-natured and peaceable, a direct synonym for friendly; split it reads as a question about being wired.

clue.text: Meaty pancake — it fills hole, mostly

indicators.note: the it word fills the gap inside the shortened hole
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a burrow is an animal's hole

explanation.surface: A filling snack that plugs a gap in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it fills hole' looks like a phrase about hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla wrapped round a filling, often meat, loosely a stuffed pancake.

clue.text: A question brought in by this organised support

indicators.note: the A and question letters are brought into the clue word

parts.note: this refers to the very thing being read, a clue

explanation.surface: A question is raised by a group of hired backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is self-referential: the thing you are reading is a CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A group hired to applaud a performer, hence paid, arranged backing.

clue.text: Special tricks in writing — and what they outperform?

parts.note: wordplay is clever verbal trickery in writing

explanation.surface: Clever writers' tricks are said to beat something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying that the pen is mightier than the sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing with blades is what the pen, and its tricks, are proverbially mightier than.

clue.text: Cautious, bringing article forward in the wrong way?

indicators.note: the article letter is brought forward to the front

parts.note: wary means cautious
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A careful person wonders if bringing something forward is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Means off course or amiss, so going in a mistaken direction.

clue.text: Number reflected American responsibility

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the number letters are reversed

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: An American looks back at a figure of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or obligation placed on someone, a duty they carry.

clue.text: United getting behind half of FA — surprised?

indicators.note: the united word goes behind the half letter
half of the two-letter abbreviation is one letter, here its second

parts.note: wed means united in marriage

explanation.surface: Manchester United backing the Football Association causes shock.
explanation.walkthrough: FA is the Football Association, and 'United' suggests a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with wonder or amazement, a near synonym of surprised.

clue.text: Description of Queen's trainer (note Queen not present) at work?

definitions.text: Description of Queen's trainer (note Queen not present) at work?

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, rearranged, once the note and queen letters are set aside

parts.note: N is a note, as in a musical scale abbreviation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A portrait of the royal horse trainer at work, without the monarch around.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N and ER out of QUEEN'S TRAINER ('not present') and rearrange the rest ('at work').
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes anything to do with horse riding, fitting someone who trains the monarch's horses.

clue.text: Merit attention being given to name

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone deserves notice for their reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve or gain it, as one gains respect, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Malevolent astronomer shunning company about moon of Jupiter

indicators.note: the shortened astronomer goes around the moon
shunning means avoiding, so the company letters are dropped

parts.note: Copernicus was the Polish astronomer of the heliocentric model
Io is one of Jupiter's large moons

explanation.surface: A spiteful stargazer avoids people and fixates on Jupiter's satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful and wicked in effect, a close synonym of malevolent.
